The journaling process operates as a dual-state feedback loop: one where settled outcomes inform posterior beliefs (journal outcome regression), and another where factor weights adjust dynamically (factor weight adjustment). These two primitives interact through a shared latent variable—model confidence—which is modulated by autopsies and pre-mortems. The stress test forward look acts as a boundary condition that constrains the validity of these regressions into future weeks. Failure modes arise when autopsies exceed threshold (breakdown regime), or when factor changes are too abrupt (non-linearity). The system maintains coherence through compliance checks that enforce structural consistency across outputs.
